relationships.subject: STING
relationships.evidence_quote: STING activation results in the production of type I IFNs (IFN-I) in immune cells and sensory neurons following infections or tissue injury

relationships.subject: Type I interferon
relationships.evidence_quote: persistent STING activation and IFN-I production reduced the excitability of TRPV1 neurons by increasing Kv4-mediated A-type currents

relationships.subject: STING
relationships.evidence_quote: constitutive activation of STING in TRPV1+ neurons led to a decrease in TRPV1, TRPA1, and TRPC3 expression, while promoting an increase in the A-type potassium (Kv) channel–regulating protein (KChIP1)

key_findings: Commentary on Defaye et al.: neuronal STING activation in TRPV1+ neurons drives IFN-I/IFNAR1 signaling that raises Kv4-KChIP1 A-type currents and promotes resolution of inflammatory thermal hyperalgesia.
Open questions include STING effects in Nav1.8+ neurons and in chronic inflammation.
